questions.stem_text: The demand curve for a perfectly competitive firm's product is

options.A: upward sloping and greater than the market demand curve.
options.B: kinked at the market price and less than the market demand curve.
options.D: downward sloping and equal to the market demand curve.
options.E: downward sloping and less than the market demand curve.

questions.stem_text: The Law of Diminishing Marginal Returns is responsible for

options.A: MC that first falls, but eventually rises, as output increases.
options.B: AP that first falls, but eventually rises, as output increases.
options.C: TC that first falls, but eventually rises, as output increases.
options.D: AVC that first rises, but eventually falls, as output increases.
options.E: MP that first falls, but eventually rises, as output increases.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - MC that first falls, but eventually rises, as output increases.

questions.stem_text: Which of the following could be used as a test for autocorrelation up to third order?
questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - The Dickey-Fuller test

options.A: when price goes up supply goes up
options.B: price and supply have no correlation
options.C: when supply goes up, demand goes down
options.E: when demand goes up, supply goes down

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - when price goes up supply goes up

questions.stem_text: Suppose that there are only two goods: x and y. Which of the following is NOT correct?

options.A: One can have comparative advantage in producing both goods.
options.B: One can have both an absolute advantage and a comparative advantage in producing x.
options.C: One can have absolute advantage and no comparative advantage in producing x.
options.D: One can have comparative advantage and no absolute advantage in producing x.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - One can have comparative advantage in producing both goods.
